title: Selective-bias screening nominates LabMol-394 antimalarial candidates
summary: A machine-learning workflow guided virtual screening for parasite N-myristoyltransferase, followed by testing of selected compounds in parasite assays. The primary preprint reports a bounded set of measured antimalarial candidates, including LabMol-394, while target assignment remains computational. This is not clinical efficacy or proof of target engagement.
ai_technology: Selective-bias virtual screening; machine-learning target/activity models
organization: Federal University of Goiás; University of Gothenburg

evidence.tested: Primary preprint full text reports tested selected candidates and parasite activity.
evidence.unknown: Exact earliest journal version and compound prior art remain open; target-specific binding is not experimentally established.
evidence.ai_role: Model-based selective-bias workflow scores target/activity candidates for experimental testing.

source_review.scope: PMC-indexed primary preprint full text; PubMed primary record/abstract and affiliations. Material checked for the specific claims stated in the record.
